ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A small block with mass $\mathbf{m}$ and charge $+\mathbf{q}$ is placed on a smooth, insulating inclined plane with an angle of inclination θ. The plane is situated in a uniform magnetic field with magnetic induction B, directed perpendicularly outward from the plane of the paper, as shown in the figure. The small block starts sliding down the incline from rest, and the incline is sufficiently long. The acceleration due to gravity is g.

1. How does the magnitude of the pressure exerted by the small slider on the inclined plane change during its motion?
2. The instantaneous speed of the small block as it leaves the inclined plane;
3. The time for the small block to move on the inclined plane.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
The pressure exerted by the small block on the inclined plane becomes increasingly smaller.
$\frac{mg\cos\theta}{qB}$
$\frac{m}{qB\tan\theta}$

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A small block with mass $m$ and charge $+q$ is placed on a smooth, insulating inclined plane with an angle of inclination $\theta$. The plane is situated in a uniform magnetic field with magnetic induction $B$, directed perpendicularly outward from the plane of the paper, as shown in the figure. The small block starts sliding down the incline from rest, and the incline is sufficiently long. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$. 1. What is the instantaneous speed of the small block as it leaves the inclined plane? 3. What is the time for the small block to move on the inclined plane?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The figure shows a triangular inclined plane whose sloping surface rises to the right and makes an angle θ with the horizontal. A small block is drawn on the sloped surface near the upper right. The background contains repeated dot symbols and the label B, indicating a uniform magnetic field perpendicular outward from the page. Reasoning: Choose one axis along the incline downward and one axis perpendicular to the plane outward from the surface. The block has charge +q and starts from rest on a smooth insulating plane, so there is no friction. As the positive block slides down the incline, its velocity is along the plane downward. With B outward from the page, the right-hand rule gives the magnetic force qvB perpendicular to the incline and away from the plane. Therefore this magnetic force reduces the normal force. While the block is still in contact with the plane, the normal-direction force balance is N + qvB = mg cosθ, so N = mg cosθ − qBv. Since the speed v increases during the motion, N decreases. The pressure exerted by the block on the plane has the same magnitude as the normal force, so it becomes increasingly smaller, reaching zero when the block leaves the plane. Along the incline, the magnetic force has no component, so the acceleration is constant: ma = mg sinθ, hence a = g sinθ. Starting from rest, v = g sinθ · t. The block leaves the plane when N = 0: mg cosθ − qBv = 0, so v_leave = mg cosθ/(qB). Substituting this into v = g sinθ · t gives t = [mg cosθ/(qB)]/[g sinθ] = m/(qB tanθ).

The background contains repeated dot symbols and the label B, indicating a uniform magnetic field perpendicular outward from the page.

With B outward from the page, the right-hand rule gives the magnetic force qvB perpendicular to the incline and away from the plane. Therefore this magnetic force reduces the normal force.

While the block is still in contact with the plane, the normal-direction force balance is
N + qvB = mg cosθ,
so
N = mg cosθ − qBv.
